policy: Standardize semantics, safety, authority, lifecycle and evidence before syntax. Classify product runtime components with orthogonal axes (class, required scope, boundary role, state kind/recovery class, maturity and distribution). Conformance is not maturity and publication is not verified promotion. Do not force identical product topology where it adds coupling or breaks a simpler domain-native interface.

conformance_statuses.ADAPT: Same semantic contract with product-native syntax/layout; mapping must be explicit.
conformance_statuses.PRODUCT_SPECIFIC: Common contract is insufficient; product owns a justified additional contract without weakening common invariants.
conformance_statuses.N_A: The control does not apply to this product/scope; rationale required.
conformance_statuses.PASS: Deliberately not standardized because forced unification creates more complexity/risk than value; rationale and revisit trigger required.

common_cli.rule: Use lifecycle-verb form only for true product lifecycle operations; use noun/verb for domain resources. Do not create aliases merely to make products look identical.

common_flags.--help/-h: side-effect-free help; Windows-native launchers may also support /?
common_flags.--version: side-effect-free version where product has a versioned CLI
common_flags.--json: machine-readable output when the command exposes structured state/evidence
common_flags.--dry-run: must not mutate and always wins over --apply when both are supplied
common_flags.--apply: explicitly permits mutation for preview-by-default destructive/recovery commands
common_flags.--yes/-y: skips ordinary confirmation only; must never bypass hard safety identity/containment/precondition gates

common_cli.numeric_policy: Existing products may retain numeric assignments for compatibility. New surfaces must publish a semantic->numeric map and avoid conflicting meanings inside one product.
common_cli.flag_applicability: Each common concern is classified REQUIRED / OPTIONAL / N_A / PASS per public command or command family. N_A/PASS requires rationale; do not add irrelevant flags merely for symmetry.
common_cli.json_output_rule: When --json is offered, stdout MUST contain only the declared machine-readable format; human diagnostics use stderr or structured fields. Collections should normally be [] rather than null; null/absent/unknown semantics must be schema-defined.

exit_semantic_definitions.SUCCESS: Requested effect completed according to contract.
exit_semantic_definitions.USAGE: CLI syntax/argument/input-schema error before the requested operation begins.
exit_semantic_definitions.DECLINED: The user intentionally chose not to proceed (for example ordinary confirmation = No).
exit_semantic_definitions.PRECONDITION_FAILED: Required precondition was not met before mutation/execution began.
exit_semantic_definitions.BLOCKED: Policy, safety, fencing, authority or containment deliberately prevented the operation.
exit_semantic_definitions.VERIFICATION_FAILED: The operation ran but required postcondition/evidence verification failed.
exit_semantic_definitions.ROLLED_BACK: Mutation began and was deterministically compensated/rolled back; intended final effect was not committed.
exit_semantic_definitions.RUNTIME_FAILED: External runtime/provider/process/I/O execution failed without an internal contract defect.
exit_semantic_definitions.INTERNAL_ERROR: Unexpected product defect or unclassified internal failure.

controls.name: CLI grammar and command surface
controls.contract: Unify semantic command grammar, applicable common flag meaning, non-destructive defaults and stable command discovery; exact hierarchy may adapt to product domain and irrelevant flags must not be added for symmetry.

controls.name: Help and discoverability
controls.contract: Help is side-effect free, available at root and public commands, generated or checked against the public command SSOT, and includes usage/options/examples/exit semantics.

controls.name: Exit semantic classes
controls.contract: Every public command maps outcomes to stable semantic classes. Numeric codes may be product-specific to preserve compatibility, but meanings must be documented and machine-testable.

controls.name: Configuration precedence
controls.contract: Configuration sources have one explicit precedence chain and explicit per-key merge semantics (default REPLACE). Defaults are declarative; secrets are separated; absent/null/empty/unknown semantics are explicit and unknown/absent values are never coerced into zero/false/healthy.

controls.name: Filesystem and state classes
controls.contract: Physical paths may differ. Every persisted/ephemeral item declares a State Kind and an orthogonal Recovery Class; authoritative, durable-derived, rebuildable, ephemeral and external state are not conflated.

controls.name: Schema and versioning
controls.contract: Structured contracts use versioned schemas, reject unsupported major versions, preserve unknown data only where contract allows, and migrate transactionally.

controls.name: Component ownership and dependencies
controls.contract: Every component declares runtime plane, lifecycle/ownership class (Core, Module, Extension, Generated View, External), required scope and an independent boundary role (none/adapter/provider/exporter). Dependency direction is explicit and acyclic at authority boundaries.

controls.name: Extension and provider contract
controls.contract: Modules/extensions and interchangeable providers/adapters/exporters declare only the contracts needed for their role. Optional Extensions reach authoritative state only through public ports; provider-specific state stays outside Core; failure isolation is not claimed as a security sandbox.

controls.name: Observation and diagnostics
controls.contract: Operational facts preserve evidence state and freshness. Diagnostic views are read-only; repair/restart/routing are separate actions or extensions.

controls.name: Logging and evidence
controls.contract: Human-visible operational output has a reproducible evidence path; structured evidence carries timestamp, candidate/source identity and schema version. Console-to-file exact mirroring is required for evidence-oriented scripts where practical.

controls.name: Security and containment
controls.contract: External side effects fail closed, secrets are excluded or isolated by construction, restore/import paths are canonically contained, writable host mounts are minimized, trust boundaries are explicit, and third-party/downloaded artifacts have provenance/integrity policy appropriate to risk.

controls.name: Migration, compatibility and deprecation
controls.contract: Migrations are explicit, replayable/rollback-aware as applicable; deprecated surfaces have replacement, warning/removal policy; historical names do not force historical architecture to return.

controls.name: Recursive MECE test and interaction assurance
controls.contract: Requirements declare applicable dimensions; positive/negative/boundary/fault/meta cases, state transitions, exceptions and high-risk interactions close with no unexplained OPEN state. Public mutations document retry/idempotency/duplicate/crash semantics where applicable.

controls.name: Build, release and gate evidence
controls.contract: Build candidates are identity-bound and built once. Blocking gates require a valid current PASS for the exact candidate; queued/running/cancelled/stale/unavailable evidence never counts as PASS. Publication status is separate from verification maturity; stable promotion must promote the same verified artifact.

controls.name: Documentation and SSOT projection
controls.contract: Canonical facts/contracts have one machine-readable or canonical source where feasible; human docs are generated or drift-tested. Conformance, maturity and distribution/publication are separate axes and product-specific prose cannot override executable contract truth.

forced_unification_guardrails: Do not rename stable commands solely for cross-product symmetry.
Do not share a database/schema between products solely to reuse code.
Do not make an optional provider/extension a Core dependency.
Do not unify numeric exit codes if doing so breaks scripts; unify semantic classes first.
Do not duplicate product-specific safety logic into a generic layer until at least two products need the same invariant.
Do not treat COMPLY/ADAPT as proof that a capability is implemented; maturity/evidence is a separate axis.
Do not model Adapter and Provider as mutually exclusive product-extension types; they are boundary roles orthogonal to component lifecycle/ownership.
Do not confuse publication/distribution with verification or stable promotion.
Do not collapse State Kind and Recovery Class into one taxonomy.
Do not classify delivery/test harnesses as product runtime components solely because they use the same provider technology.

maturity_statuses.PLANNED: Intent accepted; detailed design/implementation not frozen.
maturity_statuses.DESIGN_FROZEN: Contracts/boundaries frozen enough to begin RED/TDD; not implementation evidence.
maturity_statuses.IMPLEMENTED: Implementation exists but required assurance evidence may be incomplete.
maturity_statuses.VERIFIED: Declared verification scope has valid current PASS evidence bound to the exact candidate/input identity.
maturity_statuses.DEPRECATED: Still supported during migration but scheduled for replacement/removal.
maturity_statuses.RETIRED: No longer supported/active; historical evidence may remain.

config_value_semantics.ABSENT: No value supplied at this layer; continue precedence lookup/inherit.
config_value_semantics.NULL: Explicit null only when schema permits clear/unset semantics; never silently treated as absent.
config_value_semantics.EMPTY_STRING: A real empty string unless schema explicitly forbids or defines clear semantics.
config_value_semantics.EMPTY_ARRAY: An explicitly empty collection; distinct from absent/unknown.
config_value_semantics.UNKNOWN: Observed fact is not known; never coerce to zero/false/healthy/unlimited.

config_merge_policy.rule: Any non-REPLACE key must declare its merge algorithm explicitly in schema/config metadata; implicit deep merge is forbidden.

distribution_statuses.NOT_PUBLISHED: No external/public distribution exists for this artifact/candidate.
distribution_statuses.CANDIDATE: Identity-frozen artifact/candidate exists for gate evaluation but is not a stable publication.
distribution_statuses.PUBLISHED: Artifact/version is externally visible/distributed; this does not imply required gates passed before publication.
distribution_statuses.PROMOTED: The same identity-bound candidate/artifact passed required gates and was promoted to the declared stable channel.
distribution_statuses.WITHDRAWN: Previously distributed artifact/version has been withdrawn/deactivated from the declared channel.
